questions.stem: A client is admitted with active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which precautions should the nurse implement?

options.label: A
options.text: Droplet precautions with a surgical mask when within three feet of the client
options.rationale: Droplet precautions are for large-particle pathogens such as influenza; tuberculosis spreads by tiny airborne droplet nuclei that a surgical mask does not filter.

options.label: B
options.text: Airborne precautions in a negative-pressure room with an N95 respirator
options.rationale: Tuberculosis is spread by airborne droplet nuclei, so the client needs a negative-pressure room and staff must wear a fit-tested N95 respirator.

options.label: C
options.text: Contact precautions with a gown and gloves for all care
options.rationale: Contact precautions address organisms spread by touch, such as MRSA or C. difficile, and do nothing to stop airborne transmission.

questions.teachingPoint: Airborne precautions (negative pressure, N95) are required for tuberculosis, measles and varicella; droplet and contact precautions are not enough.

questions.stem: A client has soft wrist restraints ordered because of repeated attempts to pull out a central line. Which nursing action is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Secure the restraint ties to the side rails with a quick-release knot
options.rationale: Ties must go to the bed frame, never the side rails, because moving the rail can tighten the restraint and injure the client.

options.label: B
options.text: Check circulation, skin and range of motion at least every two hours and release the restraints periodically
options.rationale: Regular monitoring of circulation and skin plus scheduled release prevents nerve damage, skin breakdown and contractures, and is required by restraint standards.

options.label: C
options.text: Keep the restraints in place until the provider renews the order in seventy-two hours
options.rationale: Restraint orders must be renewed far more often than every seventy-two hours and restraints are removed as soon as they are no longer needed.

questions.teachingPoint: Restraints are a last resort: tie to the frame with a quick-release knot, check the client frequently, release regularly and use the least restrictive option.

questions.stem: The nurse discovers a small fire in a wastebasket in an occupied client room. What should the nurse do first?

options.label: A
options.rationale: Sounding the alarm is the second step; the client in immediate danger must be moved away from the fire first.

options.label: B
options.text: Move the client out of the room
options.rationale: In the RACE sequence, rescuing anyone in immediate danger comes before alarm, containment and extinguishing.

options.label: C
options.text: Extinguish the fire with the nearest extinguisher
options.rationale: Extinguishing is the last step of RACE and is attempted only after people are safe and the alarm has been raised.

questions.teachingPoint: RACE: Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Extinguish. Client safety always comes before fighting the fire.
